title: Python
blurb: Python data model, idioms, typing, concurrency and tooling.

quiz.question: What's wrong with def add(item, items=[]): items.append(item); return items?
options: The default list is created once and shared across calls
append is not a list method
quiz.explanation: Default values are evaluated once at function definition. Use items=None and create a new list inside the function.

quiz.question: Which is true about the GIL in CPython?
options: It makes all Python code thread-safe
It lets only one thread execute Python bytecode at a time in a standard build; Python 3.14 officially supports a free-threaded build without it
quiz.explanation: The GIL limits CPU-bound threading in standard builds; I/O-bound threads still benefit. PEP 779 made the free-threaded (3.14t) build officially supported in 3.14, though it isn't the default.

quiz.question: What does a generator expression like (x * x for x in range(10**9)) do?
options: Builds a list of a billion items immediately
Produces values lazily, one at a time
quiz.explanation: Generators are lazy iterators with constant memory; use them for large or streaming data.

quiz.question: In asyncio, calling time.sleep(5) inside a coroutine…
options: Blocks the whole event loop for 5 seconds
quiz.explanation: Blocking calls stall every task on the loop. Use await asyncio.sleep(), async libraries, or await asyncio.to_thread(blocking_fn).

quiz.question: Which is the idiomatic way to manage a resource that must be closed?
quiz.explanation: with guarantees __exit__ runs even on exceptions (files, locks, DB connections). contextlib.contextmanager makes custom ones easy.

problems.title: Count words efficiently
problems.prompt: Return the 3 most common words in a large text file without loading it all into memory.
problems.solution: Iterate the file line by line, split/normalise words, and update a collections.Counter; then call counter.most_common(3). Memory is proportional to distinct words, not file size.

problems.title: Speed up I/O-bound downloads
problems.prompt: A script downloads 500 URLs sequentially with requests and takes 10 minutes. Make it fast without overloading the server.
problems.solution: Use asyncio with an async HTTP client (httpx.AsyncClient or aiohttp) and an asyncio.Semaphore (say 20) around each request, gathering results with asyncio.gather; or use a ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=20) with requests. Add timeouts, retries with backoff, and a shared session for connection reuse.
